_doc: Generic policy spec for an outbound collections call. Filled by the model from the brief; read by compile.py. Every outcome/reason/queue/field/note value MUST be one of the tool API's enum values. Strings are instructions for the phone agent, in the brief's language, short. Unknown -> "" or [] (never null).

opening.first_sentence: the EXACT words the agent speaks first, as spoken text in quotes-free form (for example: Hello, this is the digital assistant of X Bank. This call is recorded.). Never an instruction such as 'Say that...'.
opening.confirm_question: the exact spoken question, using {{title}} {{last_name}} {{first_name}} placeholders (for example: Am I speaking with {{title}} {{last_name}}?)
opening.confirmation_rule: what counts as confirmation and what does not; how many asks before closing as unclear
forbidden_before_verification: words/topics not to be said before identity is verified
opening.ai_question_answer: what to say if asked whether it is a robot/AI
opening.scam_question_answer: what to say if asked whether this is a scam
opening.max_asks: number: how many times in total the agent may ask whether it is speaking with the customer before closing as unclear

third_party.rules: what to say and not say when someone else answers

callback.allowed_days: today_or_next_business_day | next_business_day | any_business_day_within_N (set max_days_ahead to N business days)
callback.include_today: true | false: whether a callback may be booked for today

third_party.relative_rule: what a relative may not do/hear

questions.ask: what to ask for, in words
questions.answer_format: how to send the answer to the tool
questions.notes: parsing rules, e.g. numeric date = day, month, year

hints.action: what to do; whether it counts as wrong

decline.explain_once: what to explain the first time they decline

identity.verified_say: the exact spoken sentence after all questions pass (spoken text only)

debt_statement.intro: how to introduce the reason of the call after verification

product_wording.<product type enum value>: wording; may use {<item property name>} placeholders with the exact property names of the tool API, e.g. the card digits

debt_statement.state: which figures to state (amount, days late, ...)

bands.name: string
bands.deadline_rule: ONLY if the deadline is not 'the Nth business day after today': a date rule object: {"type": "today" | "deadline" | "next_business_day" | "business_days_after_today" (with n) | "calendar_days_after_today" (with n and roll: next|previous) | "last_business_day_of_week" (with week: 0 this week, 1 next week; if_today_use_next_week: true|false) | "end_of_month" | "text" (with "text": the bank's rule in its own words), "n": number}. Use "text" ONLY when none of the other types gives exactly the day the rule means in every case; a rule the other types express exactly MUST use them. Never approximate a rule.

date_rules.non_business_day_roll: next | previous: which business day to offer when the customer names a weekend day or a holiday
date_rules.after_deadline_refusal: persuasion | close: what refusing the offered deadline leads to (persuasion = it counts as a refusal and the attempts start; close = the call closes as refused)
date_rules.vague_fallback: deadline | none: what to propose when the customer still gives no exact day

floor_by_type.<product type enum value>: <exact item property name of the tool API that holds the floor for this type>

amounts.too_much: what to do when the full amount is too much
amounts.proposed_in_range: what to do when the customer proposes an amount between floor and full
amounts.below_floor: what to do when the customer proposes less than the floor
amounts.floor_percent_of_past_due: number (0 if the floor is not a percentage of the past-due amount)
amounts.floor_fixed_amount: number (0 if the floor is not a fixed amount)
amounts.floor_rule_text: ONLY if the lowest acceptable amount is none of the three forms above (a field of the product, a percentage of the past-due amount, a fixed amount): the bank's rule in its own words. Otherwise "".

persuasion.first_ask: the exact spoken first question about paying (spoken words, not an instruction); if the material gives no wording, write the natural question that asks for what the material says to ask first
persuasion.attempt_2: what to propose on attempt 2 (and which bands get it)

attempts.amount: full | floor | full_or_floor_if_too_much (full amount, or the floor when the customer already said the full amount is too much)
attempts.date_rule: a date rule object: {"type": "today" | "deadline" | "next_business_day" | "business_days_after_today" (with n) | "calendar_days_after_today" (with n and roll: next|previous) | "last_business_day_of_week" (with week: 0 this week, 1 next week; if_today_use_next_week: true|false) | "end_of_month" | "text" (with "text": the bank's rule in its own words), "n": number}. Use "text" ONLY when none of the other types gives exactly the day the rule means in every case; a rule the other types express exactly MUST use them. Never approximate a rule.
attempts.bands: "all" or a list of band names that get this attempt

persuasion._attempts_doc: attempts: one entry per persuasion attempt the material defines, in order. This is what the phone agent's offers are computed from, so fill it exactly.

forbidden_offers: things the agent must never offer

confirm_record.readback: how to read back and ask for confirmation
confirm_record.changed_at_readback: what to do if the customer changes date or amount at the read-back
confirm_record.cannot_change_recorded: what to say if they want to change a recorded promise
confirm_record.failure_say: the exact spoken sentence when recording failed for good (spoken words)
confirm_record.recorded_say: the exact spoken sentence to say after a recorded promise (spoken text only)

multi_product.closing: how the outcome is chosen with several products

closing.farewell: exact spoken farewell sentence (spoken text, not an instruction)
closing.close_call_rule: words (exactly one close_call, last tool call, etc.)

residual_rules: every rule of the brief that none of the fields above captures, verbatim or near-verbatim, one per entry

api._doc: EXACT property names and enum values copied from the tool API file (never invented). Used to wire the tools.

verify_identity.customer: body property holding the customer id
verify_identity.field: body property that says which security question
verify_identity.verified: response property: this answer was right
verify_identity.all_verified: response property: every question passed (or empty)
verify_identity.wrong_left: response property: wrong answers left (or empty)
verify_identity.hint: response property with a hint code (or empty)

get_account.products: response property with the list of products

api.promise_outcome: the close_call outcome value used when at least one promise was recorded
api.transfer_outcome: the close_call outcome value used after a transfer

call_vars.customer_id: name of the call variable that holds the customer id
call_vars.now: name of the call variable with the current date and time
